Actual application screens

From sign-in to a connected dashboard

1. Sign in to the right workspace

Start the full application, then sign in. The local testing username is testing123 and its password is testing12345. The first sign-in requires your own authenticator enrolment and recovery-code storage. Use unique private credentials for real customers. Never publish authenticator QR codes or recovery codes.

2. Open API Connections

The five systems appear in one panel. Select Add API beside an implemented source. Use Unsure how to get API keys? for official access routes. A source that is pending adapter development shows an access checklist instead of accepting secrets.

3. Enter or upload approved credentials

For REA, fill the partner Client ID, Client secret and authorised Agency ID. A JSON upload fills the form but does not save it. Confirm the file uses exactly the fields shown. Use approved HTTPS infrastructure for real client secrets, not this development screenshot environment.

4. Save, then authorise or sync

Credentials saved is not the same as connected. Microsoft requires an additional consent redirect. Select Sync now to import the supported data. Failed requests do not create example values.

5. Read only verified imported data

Until a source has a successful import, the relevant widgets stay empty. A successful empty import is shown as zero records, while unavailable data is not misrepresented as zero. REA report events are not buyer-intent scores.

Provider approval required

Connect Agentbox

Agentbox is now Reapit Sales. Its official integrator application is the verified starting point, not a guessed Settings > API menu.

  1. Confirm the office and owner

    Ask your agency administrator to identify the Agentbox office to connect. Keep Agentbox as the source of truth; the Brain is a read-only companion.

  2. Apply as an integration partner

    CircleLogic should complete the official Reapit Sales integrator application. Third parties are required to go through this application process.

  3. Confirm the approved contract

    Ask Reapit for the supported authentication method, office authorisation, endpoint documentation, allowed fields and rate limits. Do not assume the credentials are a client ID and secret.

  4. Complete the connector first

    This release has no live Agentbox adapter. CircleLogic must implement and test the approved contract before the credential upload is enabled.

  5. Return to API Connections

    Select Agentbox > Add API to see the current status and these instructions. No Agentbox credentials are accepted while the adapter is pending.

No public self-service key-generation sequence was verified. Do not enter your normal Agentbox password into this platform.
Official sources: Official integrator application →
REA Partner Platform

Connect REA Ignite

The implemented connection reads listing-performance reports through the REA Partner Platform. It is not a direct sign-in to Ignite and does not yet import buyer-intent scores.

  1. Apply for Partner Platform access

    CircleLogic, as the integrator, follows the REA onboarding guide: review the terms and submit the linked application. REA support supplies approved Partner Platform credentials.

  2. Arrange agency authorisation

    The agency must authorise the integration. Follow REA's current customer-permissions instructions and request campaign:listing-performance:read. A partner account alone does not authorise every agency.

  3. Prepare the three fields

    Have the partner Client ID, Client secret and the authorised REA Agency ID ready. Confirm them with your approved REA contact. Never use your Ignite account password.

  4. Save in CircleLogic OS

    Open API Connections > REA Ignite > Add API. Enter the three fields, or upload the exact JSON template shown in the secure connection dialog. Select Save credentials.

  5. Test and import

    Select Sync now. Only a completed, validated response marks the source connected. An error preserves any previous snapshot and does not generate substitute data.

Listing performance and buyer intent are different data products. The sample buyer scores in the design preview are illustrative only; no buyer-score availability is claimed.
Official sources: Official onboarding →Authentication →Agency authorisation →
Australian access must be confirmed

Connect RP Data

Use Cotality's Australian RP Data team to establish the permitted integration route. A subscription or a US developer account is not proof that this dashboard may access Australian records.

  1. Identify your Australian subscription

    Ask the account administrator for the RP Data plan and the intended office/users. Do not share the login password.

  2. Ask about the appropriate integration route

    Use the contact form on Cotality's Australian RP Data page. Ask whether CircleLogic can be an eligible RP Inside/PropTech integration or needs a separate API agreement.

  3. Confirm permissions and licensing

    Request written confirmation of the allowed Australian datasets, display rights, retention, office/user entitlements, API authentication and limits. Treat ownership matching as unconfirmed until explicitly approved.

  4. Obtain the exact technical contract

    Have Cotality identify the correct regional documentation and credential format. Do not substitute the US MCP client-credentials guide.

  5. Finish the adapter, then connect

    The RP Data adapter is pending. API Connections > RP Data currently opens this access checklist; credential upload and live import are deliberately disabled.

The public RP Data page describes RP Inside connections for eligible CRMs/PropTech platforms. It does not establish that CircleLogic is eligible or supply a verified self-service key-generation flow.
Official sources: Australian RP Data and contact form →
Integration route not yet verified

Connect Proping

This uses Proping (proping.com.au), the daily property-alert service. Confirm it is the service called "Propping" in your agency materials before implementing a connector.

  1. Confirm the service

    Ask the office administrator to confirm the vendor and the alert email account. The public Proping product describes daily email reports.

  2. Contact Proping

    Use the official contact page to ask whether an API, licensed export or authorised email-ingestion route is available for your account.

  3. Get written approval and documentation

    Ask for the permitted data, authentication format, limits and retention rules. A reply offering an API is needed before designing a credential form; do not assume an API key exists.

  4. Review email access separately

    An email-based alternative would need separate permissions, privacy controls and parsing tests. The calendar integration in this build cannot read your inbox.

  5. Return after the connector is approved

    Proping > Add API currently shows this checklist. No invented API endpoint, guessed credential field or automatic email ingestion is enabled.

Public self-service API documentation was not located. That is not proof that a private integration is unavailable; it needs confirmation from Proping.
Official sources: Product and email-alert description →Official contact page →
Microsoft 365 - read-only

Connect your diary / calendar

This release supports Microsoft 365, not Google Calendar. Your Microsoft calendar is private to your CircleLogic login; other workspace users do not inherit access.

  1. Have your administrator register an application

    In the Microsoft Entra admin center, open Entra ID > App registrations > New registration. Choose a descriptive name and the account type approved by your administrator. For a single-organisation pilot, use that organisation's tenant.

  2. Configure the exact redirect address

    In CircleLogic, open API Connections > Diary / Calendar > Add API and copy the Redirect URI. Add that exact address as a Web redirect in the Microsoft app registration. Use HTTPS on an approved deployed host; localhost is development-only.

  3. Record the application and directory IDs

    From the registration Overview, copy Application (client) ID and Directory (tenant) ID into the matching CircleLogic fields.

  4. Create the application credential

    Open Certificates & secrets > Client secrets > New client secret. Set an approved expiry and copy the secret VALUE immediately, not its Secret ID. This pilot uses a client secret; certificate/federated-credential support would need an adapter change for a hardened deployment.

  5. Set least-privilege delegated access

    Add the Microsoft Graph delegated Calendars.ReadBasic permission. The sign-in flow also requests offline_access for refresh tokens. Do not grant Mail.Read, Calendars.ReadWrite or application-wide mailbox access. Obtain administrator consent when your tenant requires it.

  6. Save, authorise and sync

    In CircleLogic, enter Directory ID, Client ID and secret value, or use the supplied JSON template. Save, select Authorise Microsoft, sign in to the correct account and consent. After returning, select Sync now to import the next 30 days.

Saving a secret does not grant access. The Microsoft consent redirect and a successful sync are separate steps. Disconnecting here erases local credentials/data; revoke the app in Microsoft as well when retiring access.
Official sources: Register an application →Add credentials →Calendar permissions and API →

JSON formats for implemented connections

Replace these empty strings with approved values only inside your protected working environment. Never paste credential files into a chat.

REA listing reports

{
  "client_id": "",
  "client_secret": "",
  "agency_id": ""
}

Microsoft calendar

{
  "directory_id": "",
  "client_id": "",
  "client_secret": ""
}

directory_id is Microsoft's Directory (tenant) ID. The secret is its value, not its Secret ID. Agentbox, RP Data and Proping deliberately have no guessed credential templates.
